items.title: should answered sit on the ask line?
body: On the ask line's dividing rule, at its right end. Decisions then sat on the open questions' rule the same way, so one pattern held across the page: a heading rule names what is behind a key and shows its state.

items.title: can a thing have two kinds?
body: No. When something seems to need two kinds, it is two linked things.

B3 Group Design Project is a course on Canvas, and 3YP is the repo where you do its work: two items with a link between them, which is why 3YP felt like it belonged in three places. One kind each, joined by links, keeps the backend's rules simple.
links: the taxonomy decision: one kind per thing

items.title: are tutorial sheets their own type, or coursework?
body: Their own type, sheet, alongside coursework. Both are tasks linked to a course, and both can carry a deadline, which any task can have.
Sheets are separate because they are planned differently: about five hours in two or three blocks, every week, where coursework needs its own estimate. Merging them would lose that.
links: the taxonomy decision: a task's type is sheet, coursework, admin or chore

items.title: what is the difference between goals and threads?
body: They are unrelated. A goal is a purpose for learning, such as Jump internship preparation. A mail thread is an email conversation.
An earlier table said "thread (keryx)", and that bracket was the confusion: it named the app that stores mail, which plays no part in labelling.

items.title: is the taxonomy global?
body: Yes. Every item, in every project and every app, carries two independent labels: its area (where it belongs in your life) and its kind (what shape of thing it is).
Both are defined once in the shared root and read by everything. The brackets naming kairos or keryx only said which app stores a thing, so they are gone.
links: the taxonomy decision, with the full grid of areas by kinds

items.title: what is the failed glyph?
body: The Nerd Font symbol that marks a failed job or session, such as a tablet push that hit the rate limit. It should pair with kairos's done box.

kairos's done box is the outline style (md-checkbox_marked_outline), so the matching failed glyph is md-close_box_outline, the one the plan named. An earlier note had suggested the filled box by mistake.
